definition: An armistice is a formal agreement between warring sides to stop fighting.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word armistice. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know armistice should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: The armistice signed in a railway carriage at Compiègne silenced the Western Front at eleven o'clock on November 11, 1918.
A ceasefire is weaker than an armistice: it quiets the guns for a stretch or a sector, while an armistice binds every front under one signed, formal halt.
Peace goes further than an armistice — an armistice only stops the shooting while the war legally continues; peace ends the war itself, with borders drawn and treaties signed.

A truce is any agreed pause in the fighting — it can be local, informal, even unspoken, and as short as an afternoon. An armistice is the formal version: negotiated, signed, and binding across the whole war.
